title: Private: install audit-exporter components + values flags + upgrade notes
author: Diego Santos
release_notes: Private deployments can now enable SIEM-ready Audit Export (beta) via installer values. Adds opt-in install + health wiring for audit-export control-plane + worker, plus documentation on required egress and secret configuration.
description: Context: This wires the SIEM-ready audit export pipeline into the Private installer so Private customers can run the same exporter components we use in Hosted/Dedicated. This PR adds Helm wiring, installer flags, and upgrade/migration notes. The feature remains disabled by default and requires the per-tenant/server-side feature flag to be enabled (handled in the control plane repo). What’s included: (1) New optional chart components: audit-export service (control plane) + audit-export-worker deployment, (2) values.yaml flags for enabling/disabling and for destination connector configuration (Splunk HEC / Datadog logs / S3), (3) external secrets integration hooks for destination credentials (Kubernetes Secret refs only; no plaintext values in values.yaml), (4) NetworkPolicy and egress notes for Splunk/Datadog endpoints, (5) Health endpoint wiring into installer smoke checks, (6) Upgrade notes and a small migration for required RBAC/ServiceAccounts. Non-goals: enabling customer-specific sinks, historical backfill, or any schema changes. Rollout: safe to ship; defaults to disabled; can be enabled per environment by updating the Private values file + restarting the affected workloads.
commits: installer/charts: add audit-export service + worker templates (gated by .Values.auditExport.enabled)
installer/values: introduce auditExport.* values (sinks, resources, egress, secrets refs)
installer/docs: add Private install notes for SIEM audit export (beta) + required egress
installer/smoke-tests: add readiness checks for audit-export endpoints when enabled
security: add NetworkPolicy rules and tighten serviceAccount RBAC for exporter pods
implementation_notes: Configuration (values.yaml): auditExport.enabled (default false); auditExport.mode=cluster|namespaced; auditExport.worker.replicas; auditExport.queue (defaults to internal durable queue service already deployed in Private); auditExport.sinks.splunk.enabled / .datadog.enabled / .s3.enabled; auditExport.secrets.* references (existingSecretName + keys). Credentials: this PR only supports Secret refs (e.g., splunkHecTokenSecretRef) and is compatible with ExternalSecrets/Vault agents that materialize into Kubernetes Secrets. No destination tokens/keys are accepted as raw values. Egress: when audit export is enabled, cluster must allow outbound HTTPS to customer SIEM endpoints (Splunk HEC) and/or Datadog intake (if used). S3 sink requires egress to the configured S3 endpoint (AWS or S3-compatible) and KMS endpoint when SSE-KMS is enabled. Observability: exporter pods emit logs + /metrics; this PR only ensures they’re deployed and scrapeable by the existing Prometheus operator if present; dashboard import remains in observability-pack. Health: /healthz (service) and /readyz (worker) are included in installer smoke checks when auditExport.enabled=true.
upgrade_migration_notes: Upgrade notes (Private): 1) No action required if audit export remains disabled. 2) If enabling: create the required Secrets first (Splunk token / Datadog API key / S3 credentials, plus optional KMS key id), then set auditExport.enabled=true and apply the Helm upgrade. 3) Ensure NetworkPolicy/egress rules allow outbound 443 to the configured destinations; otherwise the worker will go Degraded with retry backoff. 4) If your cluster uses restricted PSP/OPA policies, allow the new ServiceAccount (redwood-audit-export) to read only the referenced Secret names (namespaced). 5) If running in air-gapped mode, only S3-compatible sinks reachable within the enclave are supported; Splunk/Datadog cloud endpoints will fail. 6) After upgrade, validate: installer smoke check should include audit-export service readiness; then use Console “Send test event” (if enabled) to verify end-to-end delivery.
review_conversation: Priya Natarajan: Can we keep this strictly opt-in? I don’t want the worker consuming resources on existing Private installs by default. Also please confirm we’re not introducing any new mandatory dependencies (DB/queue) for installs that don’t enable it. Diego Santos: Confirmed. Everything is behind auditExport.enabled=false by default. The templates are gated and the smoke check only runs when enabled. No new dependencies are installed when disabled; we re-use the existing internal durable queue service when enabled.

Hanae Suzuki: Security review: I’m concerned about credentials ending up in rendered manifests or logs. Please ensure values.yaml does not accept raw tokens/keys and that we don’t print env vars in startup logs. Also can we lock RBAC to only read specific secrets? Diego Santos: Updated to only allow Secret refs (name + key). Removed the earlier convenience fields. Also tightened RBAC: the ServiceAccount only has get on secrets in its namespace, and we document using ExternalSecrets to scope secret names. Startup logs no longer print connector config; only sink type + destination id.

Sean Gallagher: Operationally: what happens if egress is blocked? We should make sure the worker fails fast and surfaces Degraded rather than silently retrying forever without backpressure. Also, can installer smoke checks avoid hard failing if audit export is enabled but destination creds aren’t present yet (common during staged installs)? Diego Santos: Worker already classifies network/auth failures and reports destination Degraded with last_error. For smoke checks, I changed the logic to validate only service readiness + worker readiness; it doesn’t attempt a delivery. Creds validation is done via the control plane ‘test delivery’ endpoint in Console (out of scope here).

Colin O'Donnell: Private customer expectation: some will use S3-compatible storage (MinIO / GovCloud). Can we avoid hardcoding AWS endpoints, and can we document required egress for KMS when SSE-KMS is configured? Diego Santos: S3 endpoint is fully configurable (auditExport.sinks.s3.endpoint). Added doc note about S3-compatible + KMS endpoint requirements and that SSE-KMS requires access to KMS API (or equivalent) and correct IAM policy (customer-managed).

Connor O'Brien: Release: please add explicit upgrade note about the new ServiceAccount/RBAC and a reminder that this is still beta behind a feature flag. Diego Santos: Added upgrade-notes section and emphasized feature remains disabled by default + requires server-side enablement.
merge_outcome: Merged to main (squash). Follow-up work tracked in ENG-13935 for additional private install validation on restricted clusters and in PM-4821 rollout checklist.
